# Project Kestrel: Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

## Headline assessment

The Seller's package departs from our playbook on almost every material point. The most serious problem is structural. Three Seller drafting moves combine to make the general warranty limitations govern everything:

- the cl 12.3/13 "applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" rule
- the cl 9.3/12.8/20.5 "all Claims of any nature" limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance language
- folding title and capacity into the general regime

Together they would cap and time-bar fraud, title, tax and IP exposure inside a 20% cap and an 18-month window.

The cover note also says things are "addressed", "agreed", "settled" or "adequate" when the Seller's own Disclosure Letter says otherwise. We should not accept the cover note's characterisations. The Disclosure Letter is dated **22 September 2026**, about six weeks ago, so every factual point needs a refresh before we rely on it.

---

## 1. Liability architecture

### 1.1 General cap (cl 12.1): 20% / AUD 4.8m
- **Departure:** Our starting position is 25% (AUD 6.0m). 20% matches our fallback number, but the fallback can only be used with **prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying this draft**. None has been given.
- **Pushback:** Counter at 25% / AUD 6.0m. Do not concede 20% in correspondence, and do not imply flexibility, until written authority covering this specific draft exists. A matching number does not make the change cleared.

### 1.2 Thresholds (cl 12.2)
| | Seller | Playbook |
|---|---|---|
| De minimis | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 |
| Basket | AUD 250,000 | AUD 50,000 |
| Mechanic | Excess only (deductible) | First dollar once exceeded (tipping) |

- **Why it matters:** The de minimis is 5x ours, the basket is 5x ours, and the mechanic is a true deductible. Together these permanently write off the first AUD 250k of qualifying loss and screen out every claim under AUD 25k. On a AUD 24m deal that is a significant economic shift. The deductible point is the biggest of the three.
- **Pushback:** AUD 5k de minimis, AUD 50k tipping basket, recovery from the first dollar. Also confirm that related or recurring claims are aggregated for de minimis purposes.

### 1.3 General claims period: 18 months
- **Departure:** Our position is 24 months. 18 months is a fallback requiring Amelia Frost's written approval, and none has been given.
- **Pushback:** 24 months from Completion.

### 1.4 "Any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" (cl 12.3/13)
- **Why it matters:** This reverses the default. Every limitation would reach fundamental, title, tax, IP, specific indemnity, payment and covenant claims unless we carve each one out expressly. This is the "hidden general-regime override" our playbook prohibits.
- **Pushback:** Delete it. Limitations should apply only to general Warranty Claims. Each other category should have its own express regime: Title/Fundamental, Tax, IP, specific indemnities, price/payment obligations and covenants.

### 1.5 Title and capacity in the general regime ("administrative simplicity")
- **Departure:** Our playbook requires a separate regime for these: 100% cap, at least six years, and outside the basket, de minimis and any knowledge bar. Administrative simplicity is not a reason to cap title on a 100% share acquisition. If title fails, we have bought nothing, and a 20% cap would leave about 80% of the price unrecoverable.
- **Pushback:** Reject. Fundamental/Title warranties should be capped at 100% of price with a claims period of at least six years, and sit outside all thresholds and knowledge qualifiers.

### 1.6 Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5)
- **Why it matters:** As drafted, this captures **fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct**. Our playbook treats the fraud carve-out as non-waivable. No one on our side may give it up. Non-reliance and exclusive-remedy clauses that purport to cover fraud are also likely to be read down or unenforceable, which creates uncertainty we should not accept.
- **Pushback:** Add an express carve-out stating that nothing in the SPA limits or excludes liability for fraud, wilful concealment or deliberate misconduct by the Seller or its representatives. This should override all caps, thresholds, time limits, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions to the maximum extent enforceable. This point is **not negotiable**.

### 1.7 Tax / IP "settled under the general regime"
- **Departure:** These terms are **open**. Nothing has resolved them. Saying they are "settled" is an assertion, not an agreement.
- **Pushback:** Expressly record that Tax and IP terms remain open, to be negotiated as separate categories. We should not assume unlimited liability in our own favour either. Our ask is a distinct, appropriately sized regime for each.

---

## 2. Disclosure and knowledge

### 2.1 General disclosure (DL 1.1–1.2)
- **Departure:** The letter discloses everything in the whole data room "including DD-002 to DD-012", plus the Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records". Our playbook rejects whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- **Pushback:** Delete 1.1 and 1.2. Disclosure should be limited to matters **fairly disclosed** in the Disclosure Letter with enough detail for a buyer to identify their nature and scope. Data room documents should count only where specifically referenced against a particular warranty. Note that 1.2's "without limiting any specific disclosure" wording does not cure the general disclosure.
- **Paragraph 1.4 (no admission of breach, materiality or requirement):** We can accept this as non-admission wording. It must not, however, dilute any warranty, indemnity or condition, and we should add language to that effect.

### 2.2 Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3)
- **Departure:** This is a blanket bar covering the Buyer **and its advisers**, actual or constructive knowledge, and anything "discoverable from the data room or public records". It is a deemed-disclosure regime by another route, and it would undercut the specific indemnities. Those indemnities exist precisely because we already know about the underlying issues (Ironquay, DD-006).
- **Pushback:** Delete cl 8.3. If any qualifier survives, it should rest on the **Seller's** knowledge, limited to named Seller knowledge persons and subject to reasonable enquiry. Buyer knowledge must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or any specific indemnity.

---

## 3. Specific transaction issues

### 3.1 Bluefen consent (cl 3/6.3)
- **The inconsistency:** The cover note says the consent is "addressed". DL §2 says no final written consent and no evidence that the clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied. Bluefen is about AUD 3.6m of revenue, roughly 30% of FY26.
- **Departure:** The Seller offers reasonable endeavours and treats the condition as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent. That is consent-on-delivery. It ignores the 11.3 conditions, and reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a customer this material.
- **Pushback:** Make it a Condition Precedent that is satisfied only by **effective** written consent under DD-002 cl 11.2, **plus** evidence that all cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied, both before Completion. The consent must be unconditional, or subject only to conditions acceptable to the Buyer. The Seller should give a stronger endeavours obligation, and the Buyer alone should have the right to waive the CP. Ask for the current status, since the DL is six weeks old.

### 3.2 Riverlark facility (cl 2/7), about AUD 3.2m
- **Departure:** The cover note proposes a "release to be provided following Completion". DL §3 confirms the facility is not repaid and no discharge is in hand. A post-completion release is permitted only with an irrevocable undertaking **and** Amelia Frost's approval, and we have neither. On a debt-free/cash-free deal, we also need to consider the change-control provision (DD-003 cl 8.1). Completion itself may trigger default or acceleration.
- **Pushback:**
  - a current payout letter, dated close to Completion
  - repayment directly from Completion funds to Riverlark
  - executed, effective security releases delivered at Completion, including PPSR and any mortgage or charge discharges, per DD-003 cl 9.2
  - the payout amount treated as Debt in the price mechanics

  Also note that "approximately" AUD 3.2m is not a payout figure.

### 3.3 Employee bonuses (DD-005), AUD 420,000 plus on-costs
- **Departure:** The cover note says the bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised. DL §5 confirms they are absent from the funds flow, and it is silent on payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs. Our playbook prohibits a funds flow that silently excludes them. If the Company pays these after Completion, the economic cost falls on us.
- **Pushback:** Either show them as a specific funds-flow line item, deducted from price and paid through payroll at Completion, or have them expressly Seller-funded. In both cases, include payroll tax, superannuation, PAYG withholding and other triggered on-costs, and treat them as Debt or Transaction Costs. Back this with a specific indemnity for any bonus or on-cost liability not paid on that basis. We cannot accept "a matter for the Seller" without a mechanism.

### 3.4 Ironquay IP (cl 11.1)
- **Departure:** The indemnity is limited to "the specific SOW3 payment" and described as "adequate". DL §4 confirms the transfer of SOW3 Project Materials is conditional on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee (DD-004 cl 7.3). There is no receipt and no confirmatory assignment. DD-010's AUD 180,000 open item is not independently verified, and we should not assume it is right or wrong.
- **Pushback:**
  - Keep the SOW3 cure: the Seller procures payment of all outstanding SOW3 fees before Completion and delivers evidence of cleared payment plus a confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay.
  - Broaden the indemnity beyond the payment itself. It should cover any loss from the Company not owning, or not being able to use, the SOW3 Project Materials, including third-party claims, re-development and remediation costs, and any amounts above AUD 180,000.
  - Place it outside the general cap, thresholds and knowledge bar.

### 3.5 Export/privacy incident (DD-006, about 1,240 records)
- **Departure:** The cover note says it is "not expected to be material". DL §6 says scope, access and notification obligations are unknown and the investigation is preliminary. Neither document establishes immateriality.
- **Our stance:** We should assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric exposure in either direction. We should not overstate it either.
- **Pushback:** Add pre-Completion covenants requiring the Seller to:
  - preserve logs and evidence
  - complete the investigation, including access logs for the download link
  - give the Buyer regular updates and access to findings
  - consult the Buyer before any notification decision or regulator or individual communication

  Add a specific indemnity for loss arising from the incident, outside the general limitations, with no amount presumed. Ask for an update, since the DL is as at 22 September.

### 3.6 Sandbar supplier renewals (DD-008/DD-011), 3 × AUD 110k = AUD 330k
- **Departure:** The Seller labels them "ordinary-course operating costs" without support. DL §8 itself says it does not state whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course. We should not assume the opposite either: no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- **Action:** Diligence is required. We need the contracts, the timing of commitment relative to the locked-box or Accounts date, termination rights, the accrual position, the business rationale for three related renewals, and whether any were entered in contemplation of the sale. Treatment (Debt, specific indemnity, conduct-of-business covenant, or nothing) should follow the findings. Meanwhile, keep a conduct-of-business restriction on further renewals without Buyer consent.

### 3.7 Title (DD-012)
- **Departure:** The Seller treats DD-012 as evidence of title. It is a supplied internal register. DL §10 itself says it identifies the source only and does not reflect Buyer verification.
- **Pushback:** Require independent evidence, including:
  - an ASIC company extract consistent with the register
  - original or certified share certificates
  - a PPSR search against the Seller and the shares
  - confirmation of no options, rights or encumbrances over the shares
  - Seller board and shareholder approvals and authority to sell

  This should sit alongside the fundamental title warranties regime in 1.5.

### 3.8 Lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)
- The Seller's characterisation here is broadly consistent with what it discloses: a notification obligation, and an assignment restriction with no stated share-sale trigger. This is lower risk, but our own counsel should confirm both clauses. Specifically, check for any deemed-assignment or change-of-control wording in the full documents, and build lease notification into the Completion steps.

---

## 4. Process points

1. **Treat the cover note as advocacy, not fact.** Words like "addressed", "agreed", "settled", "adequate" and "not expected to be material" are assertions, and several are contradicted by the Seller's own Disclosure Letter.
2. **The source facts are stale.** The DL is as at 22 September 2026. Request a bring-down on Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay payment, DD-006 and the Sandbar renewals before we finalise the mark-up. Distinguish verified updates from Seller assertions.
3. **Authority.** Any move to the 20% cap, 18-month period, or a post-completion Riverlark release needs Amelia Frost's prior written approval identifying this draft. Until then, our mark-up should reflect the starting positions. The fraud carve-out cannot be waived by anyone.

---

## 5. Summary of recommendations

| # | Issue | Seller position | Our response |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Fraud carve-out | Limitations apply to "all Claims of any nature" | **Non-negotiable:** fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct excluded from every limitation |
| 2 | Hidden override | Limits apply to all Claims unless stated | Delete; limits apply to general warranties only; separate categories |
| 3 | Title/capacity | General cap and time limits | 100% cap, ≥6 years, outside thresholds and knowledge |
| 4 | General cap | 20% / AUD 4.8m | 25% / AUD 6.0m (no authority for fallback) |
| 5 | Thresholds | AUD 25k / AUD 250k deductible | AUD 5k / AUD 50k tipping, first dollar |
| 6 | Claims period | 18 months | 24 months (no authority for fallback) |
| 7 | Tax/IP | "Settled" under general regime | Open; separate regimes to be negotiated |
| 8 | Disclosure | Whole data room + public records | Specific, fair disclosure only |
| 9 | Buyer knowledge | Blanket bar incl. advisers and discoverable | Delete; at most named Seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never title, capacity, fraud or indemnities |
| 10 | Bluefen | Reasonable endeavours; consent-on-delivery | CP: effective consent + evidence cl 11.3 conditions met, pre-Completion |
| 11 | Riverlark | Post-Completion release | Payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, releases at Completion |
| 12 | Bonuses | Excluded from funds flow | Line item or Seller-funded, incl. on-costs; indemnity |
| 13 | Ironquay | Narrow SOW3-payment indemnity | Keep cure (pay + assignment) and broaden indemnity; AUD 180k unverified |
| 14 | DD-006 | "Not material" | Preservation, investigation, update and consultation covenants; specific indemnity; no assumed outcome |
| 15 | Sandbar | Ordinary course | Diligence first; no automatic Debt or deduction; conduct-of-business restriction |
| 16 | Title evidence | DD-012 register | Independent ASIC, PPSR, certificate and authority evidence |
| 17 | Lease/Mossvale | No consent needed | Confirm with full documents; build notification into Completion |

**Priority order for the mark-up:** the fraud carve-out and the structural override come first, then title and the fundamental regime, then Bluefen and Riverlark (deal-certainty and price), then the economic terms (cap, basket, period, bonuses), then the specific indemnities and the disclosure and knowledge architecture.

- **Departure:** This is a blanket bar covering the Buyer **and its advisers**, actual or constructive knowledge, and anything "discoverable from the data room or public records". It is a deemed-disclosure regime by another route, and it would undercut the specific indemnities. Those indemnities exist precisely because we already know about the underlying issues (Ironquay, DD-006).
- **Pushback:** Delete cl 8.3. If any qualifier survives, it should rest on the **Seller's** knowledge, limited to named Seller knowledge persons and subject to reasonable enquiry. Buyer knowledge must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or any specific indemnity.

## 3. Specific transaction issues

### 3.1 Bluefen consent (cl 3/6.3)
- **The inconsistency:** The cover note says the consent is "addressed". DL §2 says no final written consent and no evidence that the clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied. Bluefen is about AUD 3.6m of revenue, roughly 30% of FY26.
- **Departure:** The Seller offers reasonable endeavours and treats the condition as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent. That is consent-on-delivery. It ignores the 11.3 conditions, and reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a customer this material.
- **Pushback:** Make it a Condition Precedent that is satisfied only by **effective** written consent under DD-002 cl 11.2, **plus** evidence that all cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied, both before Completion. The consent must be unconditional, or subject only to conditions acceptable to the Buyer. The Seller should give a stronger endeavours obligation, and the Buyer alone should have the right to waive the CP. Ask for the current status, since the DL is six weeks old.

### 3.2 Riverlark facility (cl 2/7), about AUD 3.2m
- **Departure:** The cover note proposes a "release to be provided following Completion". DL §3 confirms the facility is not repaid and no discharge is in hand. A post-completion release is permitted only with an irrevocable undertaking **and** Amelia Frost's approval, and we have neither. On a debt-free/cash-free deal, we also need to consider the change-control provision (DD-003 cl 8.1). Completion itself may trigger default or acceleration.
- **Pushback:**
  - a current payout letter, dated close to Completion
  - repayment directly from Completion funds to Riverlark
  - executed, effective security releases delivered at Completion, including PPSR and any mortgage or charge discharges, per DD-003 cl 9.2
  - the payout amount treated as Debt in the price mechanics

  Also note that "approximately" AUD 3.2m is not a payout figure.

### 3.3 Employee bonuses (DD-005), AUD 420,000 plus on-costs
- **Departure:** The cover note says the bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised. DL §5 confirms they are absent from the funds flow, and it is silent on payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs. Our playbook prohibits a funds flow that silently excludes them. If the Company pays these after Completion, the economic cost falls on us.
- **Pushback:** Either show them as a specific funds-flow line item, deducted from price and paid through payroll at Completion, or have them expressly Seller-funded. In both cases, include payroll tax, superannuation, PAYG withholding and other triggered on-costs, and treat them as Debt or Transaction Costs. Back this with a specific indemnity for any bonus or on-cost liability not paid on that basis. We cannot accept "a matter for the Seller" without a mechanism.

### 3.4 Ironquay IP (cl 11.1)
- **Departure:** The indemnity is limited to "the specific SOW3 payment" and described as "adequate". DL §4 confirms the transfer of SOW3 Project Materials is conditional on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee (DD-004 cl 7.3). There is no receipt and no confirmatory assignment. DD-010's AUD 180,000 open item is not independently verified, and we should not assume it is right or wrong.
- **Pushback:**
  - Keep the SOW3 cure: the Seller procures payment of all outstanding SOW3 fees before Completion and delivers evidence of cleared payment plus a confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay.
  - Broaden the indemnity beyond the payment itself. It should cover any loss from the Company not owning, or not being able to use, the SOW3 Project Materials, including third-party claims, re-development and remediation costs, and any amounts above AUD 180,000.
  - Place it outside the general cap, thresholds and knowledge bar.

### 3.5 Export/privacy incident (DD-006, about 1,240 records)
- **Departure:** The cover note says it is "not expected to be material". DL §6 says scope, access and notification obligations are unknown and the investigation is preliminary. Neither document establishes immateriality.
- **Our stance:** We should assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric exposure in either direction. We should not overstate it either.
- **Pushback:** Add pre-Completion covenants requiring the Seller to:
  - preserve logs and evidence
  - complete the investigation, including access logs for the download link
  - give the Buyer regular updates and access to findings
  - consult the Buyer before any notification decision or regulator or individual communication

  Add a specific indemnity for loss arising from the incident, outside the general limitations, with no amount presumed. Ask for an update, since the DL is as at 22 September.

### 3.6 Sandbar supplier renewals (DD-008/DD-011), 3 × AUD 110k = AUD 330k
- **Departure:** The Seller labels them "ordinary-course operating costs" without support. DL §8 itself says it does not state whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course. We should not assume the opposite either: no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- **Action:** Diligence is required. We need the contracts, the timing of commitment relative to the locked-box or Accounts date, termination rights, the accrual position, the business rationale for three related renewals, and whether any were entered in contemplation of the sale. Treatment (Debt, specific indemnity, conduct-of-business covenant, or nothing) should follow the findings. Meanwhile, keep a conduct-of-business restriction on further renewals without Buyer consent.

### 3.7 Title (DD-012)
- **Departure:** The Seller treats DD-012 as evidence of title. It is a supplied internal register. DL §10 itself says it identifies the source only and does not reflect Buyer verification.
- **Pushback:** Require independent evidence, including:
  - an ASIC company extract consistent with the register
  - original or certified share certificates
  - a PPSR search against the Seller and the shares
  - confirmation of no options, rights or encumbrances over the shares
  - Seller board and shareholder approvals and authority to sell

  This should sit alongside the fundamental title warranties regime in 1.5.

### 3.8 Lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)
- The Seller's characterisation here is broadly consistent with what it discloses: a notification obligation, and an assignment restriction with no stated share-sale trigger. This is lower risk, but our own counsel should confirm both clauses. Specifically, check for any deemed-assignment or change-of-control wording in the full documents, and build lease notification into the Completion steps.

## 4. Process points

1. **Treat the cover note as advocacy, not fact.** Words like "addressed", "agreed", "settled", "adequate" and "not expected to be material" are assertions, and several are contradicted by the Seller's own Disclosure Letter.
2. **The source facts are stale.** The DL is as at 22 September 2026. Request a bring-down on Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay payment, DD-006 and the Sandbar renewals before we finalise the mark-up. Distinguish verified updates from Seller assertions.
3. **Authority.** Any move to the 20% cap, 18-month period, or a post-completion Riverlark release needs Amelia Frost's prior written approval identifying this draft. Until then, our mark-up should reflect the starting positions. The fraud carve-out cannot be waived by anyone.

## 5. Summary of recommendations

|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Fraud carve-out | Limitations apply to "all Claims of any nature" | **Non-negotiable:** fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct excluded from every limitation |
| 2 | Hidden override | Limits apply to all Claims unless stated | Delete; limits apply to general warranties only; separate categories |
| 3 | Title/capacity | General cap and time limits | 100% cap, ≥6 years, outside thresholds and knowledge |
| 4 | General cap | 20% / AUD 4.8m | 25% / AUD 6.0m (no authority for fallback) |
| 5 | Thresholds | AUD 25k / AUD 250k deductible | AUD 5k / AUD 50k tipping, first dollar |
| 6 | Claims period | 18 months | 24 months (no authority for fallback) |
| 7 | Tax/IP | "Settled" under general regime | Open; separate regimes to be negotiated |
| 8 | Disclosure | Whole data room + public records | Specific, fair disclosure only |
| 9 | Buyer knowledge | Blanket bar incl. advisers and discoverable | Delete; at most named Seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never title, capacity, fraud or indemnities |
| 10 | Bluefen | Reasonable endeavours; consent-on-delivery | CP: effective consent + evidence cl 11.3 conditions met, pre-Completion |
| 11 | Riverlark | Post-Completion release | Payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, releases at Completion |
| 12 | Bonuses | Excluded from funds flow | Line item or Seller-funded, incl. on-costs; indemnity |
| 13 | Ironquay | Narrow SOW3-payment indemnity | Keep cure (pay + assignment) and broaden indemnity; AUD 180k unverified |
| 14 | DD-006 | "Not material" | Preservation, investigation, update and consultation covenants; specific indemnity; no assumed outcome |

**Priority order for the mark-up:** the fraud carve-out and the structural override come first, then title and the fundamental regime, then Bluefen and Riverlark (deal-certainty and price), then the economic terms (cap, basket, period, bonuses), then the specific indemnities and the disclosure and knowledge architecture.
